No state promise moved: checking, activating, already-active, unconfirmed and failed are each still themselves; 'does not purchase credit' survives as 'No compra crédito'; 'completed steps have not been undone', 'do not assume rollback' and 'owning credential unchanged' all survive; no string asserts or implies a charge that did not happen. Cross-namespace consistency with the shipped es copy is proved rather than assumed: mobile.setup.corrupt_intent is byte-identical to the shipped wire.tunnel_setup.corrupt_intent, mobile.setup.in_progress differs from shipped wire.tunnel_setup.in_progress only by the same ; / . difference the two English strings have, and 'acceso telefónico' matches the shipped wire.slash.mobile rendering. The seven minors are term and idiom refinements (one money verb, one enable-verb split, one state split, one calqued title, 'nueva' for 'fresh', 'redirigir' for 'repoint', 'móvil' beside 'teléfono'); none of them inverts a state and none is a blocker or a major under the delegation's severity rule.

safety_adjacent_verdict.detail: Read as a state machine. Checking (mobile.setup.checking, applying) claims no billing or installation work has started. Activating (activating) claims the subscription is being activated at the accepted price; billing_activated / billing_activated_status claim completion and add that it has not been undone; billing_already_active claims the subscription was already active, not that this run activated it; billing_not_activated claims activation is still needed; billing_unconfirmed claims an unconfirmed outcome and forbids assuming rollback; balance and consent both deny an automatic credit purchase; activated claims the owning credential is unchanged; configuring claims the owner is not switched; failed / failed_tui / unexpected_failure all keep 'completed steps have not been undone'. Negation parity was checked for all 76 keys and no negation was dropped.

check_output.negative_controls: Detectors proved against deliberately broken in-memory copies: dropped placeholder, renamed placeholder, mangled placeholder, altered URL, renamed command, changed version, removed key, added key, flipped negation, English leftover, stray exclamation, em dash -> hyphen, ellipsis -> ascii all DETECTED; the unmutated copy reports 0 problems (no false positives). One refinement is recorded honestly: the first negation detector compared the word 'no' in en against 'no' in es and reported 5 keys (invalid_response, price_unavailable, activated, identity_unavailable, reservation_unconfirmed); reading each pair showed English encodes these as single lexemes (invalid/unavailable/unchanged/unconfirmed) that Spanish renders analytically (no válida / no está disponible / no ha cambiado / sin confirmar), so all five were detector false positives, not translation defects, and the check was changed to compare presence-of-negation with the English adjectives included.
